title: The clever monkey and the crocodile.
lines: This is a story from India, from a very old book of animal stories.
On the bank of a wide river stood a big tree.
A jamun tree, full of sweet, purple berries.
A monkey lived in that tree.
His name was Raktamukha.
That's a difficult name, so we'll just call him Monkey.
Monkey was cheerful and friendly.
He jumped from branch to branch and ate the tasty berries.
One day a crocodile came swimming up to the tree.
He was tired and he was hungry.
Monkey threw down a few berries.
Here, friend, eat up!
The crocodile ate them.
Mmm, how tasty!
Thank you!
From that day on the crocodile came back every day.
Monkey threw berries, and they talked and laughed together.
They became good friends.
The crocodile also took berries home for his wife.
But his wife was greedy.
If those berries are so sweet, she said, how sweet must that monkey's heart be!
I want to eat the monkey's heart!
Bring him to me!
The crocodile didn't want to.
Monkey was his friend.
But his wife nagged and nagged.
So the next day the crocodile said: Monkey, my wife would love to meet you.
She has made a big feast.
Jump on my back, and I'll swim you to our house on the other side.
Monkey couldn't swim, but he trusted his friend.
He jumped onto the crocodile's back.
In the middle of the river, where the water was very deep, the crocodile said: I'm sorry, Monkey.
My wife actually wants to eat your heart.
Monkey got a fright.
But he stayed calm.
He thought very fast.
Oh, he said, why didn't you tell me before?
I don't have my heart with me!
I always keep it in the tree, in a little hole.
Swim back quickly, and I'll get it.
The crocodile wasn't very clever.
Oh, he said, and he swam back to the tree.
As soon as they reached the bank, Monkey leapt into the tree with one big jump.
High, high, right up to the top branch.
Silly crocodile!
he called down.
Nobody keeps their heart in a tree!
My heart is right here in my chest.
And a real friend would never trick his friend.
The crocodile was very ashamed and swam away.
And Monkey?
He stayed in his tree, ate his berries and from then on was a bit more careful about who he trusted.
Because if you stay clever and think calmly, you can always get out of trouble.
